card.name: Passive auxiliaries in old scholarly prose
card.fires_on: The word 'be' or 'been' right after will, may, have or has in dense old academic or encyclopedic writing. It also fires on a noun just before a past participle like 'given' or 'suggested'.

modes.label: be/been after modal or have
modes.description: Passive helper word where the next word is a past participle such as detailed, suggested or proposed.
modes.example: have<< been>> suggested, most of them being en tire

modes.label: Noun before a participle
modes.description: A noun such as means, works or time that is followed by a participle or phrase of this kind.
modes.example: with the<< means>> given him, he would probably have informed

modes.label: Start of a split participle
modes.description: The first piece of a verb like propounded, inside a passive phrase.
modes.example: have been<< prop>>ounded respecting the alleged meaning of the so

card.writes: It slightly pushes toward words like add and assign, and away from words like strain and significant.
card.plain: It marks the spot in old scholarly prose where a passive verb such as 'has been proposed' is about to be completed.
